- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.16) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to counteract downward bias.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 10% below 20-day low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecast using 7-day weighted average if sentiment volatility > 0.3.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model delays correction; forecast should adjust 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
